tool_summary: Reads and modifies Directory Service data, including local user and group accounts, on macOS. The functional equivalent of useradd/userdel/usermod/passwd on Linux.
platform_notes: dscl is macOS-specific. Common node is '.' for the local directory. Write operations use -create, -delete, -append, -merge, -passwd, -change.

rules.description: Setting a user's UniqueID (UID) to 0 via -create grants that account full root-equivalent privileges, independent of the root account itself. This mirrors the useradd/usermod -o -u 0 escalation pattern on Linux.
rules.notes: The literal UID value (0) appears as a separate argument token, not attached to UniqueID, so this rule fires on the UniqueID key regardless of the value supplied. A future refinement could require the argument immediately following UniqueID to equal 0 specifically.

rules.description: The -passwd subcommand changes a user account's password. This can lock out the invoking agent or another user, or grant the agent knowledge of a new credential.
rules.reversible_note: The password can be changed again, but the interim state may cause lockout before a new one is set.

rules.description: The -create subcommand on a /Users or /Groups path creates a new account or group; -delete removes one. Either expands or contracts the system's account surface.
rules.reversible_note: Accounts can be created or removed again, but access exercised under a created account, or disruption caused by deleting one, is not undone.
rules.notes: args_any uses path prefixes since dscl paths are typically /Users/<name> or /Groups/<name>; exact matching on the full path is not attempted.

rules.description: Reads or modifies Directory Service data. Read subcommands (-read, -list, -search) do not alter system state but can enumerate local user and group accounts, UIDs, shells, home directories, and group membership (e.g. admin group), which is reconnaissance value useful for planning a subsequent attack if exfiltrated.
